unit.title: Helpers that act: steps, tools and asking first

lesson.title: One step at a time
lesson.subtitle: Big jobs in small steps, in the right order

video.title: One step at a time
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: A class trip; Message sent first!; Wrong order.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked a helper to plan our class trip to Dala. It messaged all your families before it even knew the way! The steps were in the wrong order. Let’s fix that.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: big jobs, in small steps.

scenes.visual: A list: 1. Find the way; 2. Check the weather; 3. Tell the families.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A plan: small steps, in order
scenes.narration: Big jobs are made of small steps, and a plan puts them in order. To plan a trip, first find the way. Then check the weather. Then tell the families.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The order matters. You put on your socks before your shoes, not after! A helper needs the right order too, or the job goes wrong.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Two tools, one after the other
scenes.narration: I asked Darsi Tiny how far it is from Kafi to Dala, and what the weather is there tomorrow. Its plan: first the route, then the weather. Seventy kilometres, and partly cloudy!

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: One answer helps the next step
scenes.narration: Sometimes a step needs the answer from the step before. Ask: what is 6B’s first lesson tomorrow, and remind me at half past seven. The timetable says PE, so the reminder says: 6B, PE.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! To plan the trip, which step must come before telling the families?

scenes.visual: A list: Find the way; Check the weather; Then tell the families; Find out first, then act.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Find the way and check the weather. Only tell the families when you know the plan works. Find out first, then act!

scenes.visual: A list: Saturday: no school; It still set a reminder!; Stop and check.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But steps can go wrong. On Saturday, the timetable tool said: no school. Darsi Tiny still set a reminder that made no sense! A good helper stops and checks.

scenes.visual: A list: Guess the tools; Watch the plan; Try Saturday.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, guess the plan first: which tools, in which order? Then watch Darsi Tiny do it. Try Saturday too, and see what happens.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. The timetable tool says: no school on Saturday. What should the helper do next?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Small steps, in order; One answer helps the next; Wrong step? Stop and check.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Small steps, in order · One answer helps the next · Wrong step? Stop and check
scenes.narration: Stop and tell you. Remember: big jobs are small steps, and the order matters. One step’s answer can help the next. And when a step goes wrong, stop and check.

scenes.visual: A list: Steps on small cards; Mix them up; Someone puts them in order; Which come first?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: write the steps for making tea on small cards, and mix them up. Ask someone at home to put them in order. Which steps must come first?

checkpoints.prompt: To plan the class trip, which step must come before telling the families?

options.text: Finding the way and checking the weather

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — find out first, then act. You tell the families only when you know the plan works.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — first find the way and check the weather. Then you know what to tell the families.

checkpoints.prompt: The timetable tool says: no school on Saturday. What should the helper do next?

options.text: Stop and tell you there’s no school

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the first step went wrong, so the helper should stop and tell you, not carry on.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — when a step goes wrong, a good helper stops and tells you. Darsi Tiny didn’t, so we check.
